title: Explaining fan interference call in Yankees vs. Rays ALDS Game 3: Why Anthony Volpe's hit was ruled a double - CBS Sports
description: After replay, officials ruled that a fan had reached over the wall and Volpe's home run was overturned
body:
After replay, officials ruled that a fan had reached over the wall and Volpe's home run was overturned
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:15 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        NEW YORK -- Anthony Volpe tied Game 3 of the ALDS in the sixth inning, or so he and the Yankees thought. Volpe's would-be game-tying two-run home run against the Rays on Wednesday (TB 4, NY 3) was overturned on replay and ruled fan interference. A fan clearly reached over the left field wall and got his hands on the ball. Victor Mesa Jr. was under it and attempting to make a play."When he hit it, to my eye looking out there, I was a little concerned right away because it felt like something. I wasn't sure," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said after the game. "And then seeing the replay and seeing it unfold, I thought they did the right thing. I thought they got it right."  The call was overturned and Volpe was awarded a run-scoring double. Rays manager Kevin Cash argued that the play should have been overturned into an out, but to no avail. Here's the play:
"I felt like New York got it right from my vantage point," Cash said postgame. "I haven't gone back and looked at it. The only thing I saw was what was shown on the scoreboard. I didn't think the ball was going to get out, and then New York placed the runners where they were. I don't know if he would have caught it or not caught it, the guy would have scored or not."
A side angle replay showed clear evidence that the ball would not have gone over the fence for a home run, and instead would have remained in play. MLB Rule 6.0.1(e) covers spectator interference. Here is the rule, emphasis mine:There is a difference between a ball which has been thrown or batted into the stands, touching a spectator thereby being out of play even though it rebounds onto the field and a spectator going onto the field or reaching over, under or through a barrier and touching a ball in play or touching or otherwise interfering with a player. In the latter case it is clearly intentional and shall be dealt with as intentional interference as in Rule 6.01(d). Batter and runners shall be placed where in the umpire's judgment they would have been had the interference not occurred.     In the replay center's judgment, Mesa would not have caught the ball and Volpe would have reached second base, so that's where he was placed. George Lombard Jr., the runner at first base, was allowed to score because he was running on contact with two outs. In the end, a game-tying two-run homer was turned into a double that brought New York to within one."After viewing all relevant angles, the Replay Official definitively determined the spectator interfered with the ball over the field of play," MLB's Replay Center said in a statement. "The ball would not have left the playing field nor would it have been caught. The call is OVERTURNED, there was spectator interference and no home run. Additionally, the Replay Official scored one run and placed the batter-runner at second."
That overturned run would prove costly as the Rays held on to a 4-3 lead to win Game 3 and the ALDS, eliminating the Yankees from the playoffs.

title: Grading the Yankees hot seats: After playoff elimination, could Aaron Boone, Brian Cashman be out? - CBS Sports
description: The Yankees were swept by the Rays in the ALDS and now have a long, cold winter to figure out how to fix things i
body:
The Yankees were swept by the Rays in the ALDS and now have a long, cold winter to figure out how to fix things in 2027
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:30 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For the second straight season, the New York Yankees exited the postseason in the ALDS, and for the 17th straight season, they failed to win the World Series. The Yankees were swept in the Division Series by the AL East rival Tampa Bay Rays to extend their World Series drought to 17 years, tied for the longest in franchise history. Another long offseason is upon them.Like every other team after their season ends, the Yankees will hold a press conference in the coming days to debrief and talk about the offseason ahead. General manager Brian Cashman and manager Aaron Boone will answer questions at that press conference and their futures will be a big topic. They always are, these are the Yankees, but this offseason more than most.These are not George Steinbrenner's Yankees. These are Hal Steinbrenner's Yankees and Hal is much more patient and pragmatic than his father. He doesn't hire and fire coaches willy-nilly, he won't go on talk radio to call out his players, nothing like that. That's for the best, honestly. George did more harm than good before Derek Jeter & Co. showed up in the late 1990s.
        
            
                What's next for Yankees? After ugly playoffs sweep, Aaron Boone, Aaron Judge face the biggest questions
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
That said, stability becomes stagnation at some point, and the Yankees are rapidly approaching that point, if they're not there already. Their seasons tend to play out the same way: they win a lot early, swoon through the summer months, rally late in the season, beat up on a lesser team in the postseason, then get eliminated by a superior opponent, often with silly errors involved.
When it happens once, well, that's baseball, Suzyn. When it happens every year -- seriously, this is an annual occurrence -- it points to a larger organizational issue, and Boone and Cashman are the public faces of the organization. Is either in danger of being replaced this offseason? Let's talk through it.Aaron BooneContract status: Signed through 2027Manager since: 2018Hot seat: 🔥🔥🔥      You can maybe -- maybe -- talk me into Boone's seat being a 🔥🔥🔥🔥, but it is definitely not a 🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥. Boone has the right people backing him, namely Cashman and Steinbrenner, plus his players love him. That includes captain Aaron Judge, who hasn't been shy about pushing for certain moves. We have no reason to think Boone has lost the clubhouse.
At the same time, the continued sloppy play and inability to beat higher-seeded teams in the postseason reflect poorly on Boone. That last bit isn't an exaggeration either. In Boone's nine seasons, the Yankees are 7-0 in postseason series against teams with a worse regular-season record, and 1-8 against teams with a better regular-season record. That is a rough look."Those conversations and things are for another day," Boone said after the team's elimination when asked about his job status.Nine years is a very long time for a manager. It's a long time for a manager who's led his team to the World Series. Managers have a shelf life. Messages get stale and a new voice is needed, and after nine seasons, it's not unreasonable to think the Yankees are there with Boone. Not when the same script plays out year after year after year without success.
If the Yankees fire Boone, it will be the first time they fire a manager in the middle of a contract since Stump Merrill in 1991. Buck Showalter, Joe Torre, and Joe Girardi were let go after their contracts expired. Boone has a year remaining, and, if the Yankees do fire him, it'll be out of character. Steinbrenner is very budget-conscious. Does he want to pay two managers in 2027?My hunch -- I emphasize this is only a hunch -- is that Boone will return in 2027, but without a contract extension. He'll play out the year as a lame duck, and if the Yankees lose the same way in the postseason again, that'll be it. Boone simply has too much support from the right people in the organization (Cashman, Judge, Steinbrenner) for me to expect a change at manager.Brian CashmanContract status: Expiring contractGeneral manager since: 1998 (yes, really)Hot seat: 🔥  
Cashman's seat is the opposite of hot. It's icy cold. Yes, his contract is up this offseason, but there is no reason -- I mean zero -- to think Steinbrenner is ready to make a change atop the baseball operations department. Cashman is an honorary Steinbrenner at this point. Steinbrenner trusts him implicitly and the two are very close. If Cashman wants to come back, he'll be back.Therein lies the question: Does Cashman want to return for a 30th (!) season? It's a stressful job, especially in the New York media market, and burnout could finally be settling in. We have no indication of that, but that doesn't mean it's not happening behind the scenes. This isn't a "does Steinbrenner want Cashman back?" question. It's a "does Cashman want to come back?" question.If there is a change at the top of the front office, it will most likely be made as a result of Cashman wanting to step into a less demanding role. That could mean leaving the Yankees entirely. More likely, he would be elevated to, say, president of baseball operations, and someone else would take over the day-to-day work. That someone could even be handpicked by Cashman.
(Vice president of baseball operations Tim Naehring, a longtime Cashman lieutenant, is the odds-on favorite to replace Cashman.)Cashman is successful by whatever metric Steinbrenner uses to define success. We don't know what that metric is beyond "it's not recent World Series titles, obviously." Every year, the Yankees have a winning record and a roster good enough to win the World Series. This isn't a team that is eons away from a championship, even if it sometimes feels like it.Boone is far more likely to be replaced this offseason than Cashman, and even then, I wouldn't characterize it as likely. Steinbrenner is loyal to his people, maybe even to a fault, and the status quo has remained in place too long for me to think that'll change. Boone getting a lame duck year in 2027 and Cashman returning are the most likely outcomes. Any changes would come as a surprise.

title: 2026 MLB playoffs: Winners and losers as Dodgers, Rays advance, Yankees eliminated in ALDS sweep - CBS Sports
description: MLB's postseason continued on Wednesday with four potential Division Series clinchers. Regardless of the outcomes, this will be the last
body:
MLB's postseason continued on Wednesday with four potential Division Series clinchers. Regardless of the outcomes, this will be the last day with four games this season, so enjoy it. We won't get more than two games per day moving forward.  In the National League, the Los Angeles Dodgers sent the Atlanta Braves home for good with their Game 4 win to advance to the NLCS, and the Milwaukee Brewers are trying to close out their series against the San Diego Padres. On the American League side, the Chicago White Sox suffered their first loss of the playoffs as the Cleveland Guardians staved off elimination, while the Tampa Bay Rays are trying to finish a three-game sweep over the New York Yankees.   Here are the final scores and schedule for Wednesday's postseason action:  FINAL: Guardians 9, White Sox 3 (box score); White Sox lead series 2-1FINAL: Dodgers 4, Braves 1 (box score); Dodgers win series 3-1FINAL: Rays 4, Yankees 3 (GameTracker); Rays win series 3-0LIVE: Brewers at Padres (GameTracker); Brewers lead series 2-1To sum up all the Division Series action, we're here to declare a winner and loser from each of the four Wednesday contests. You can find those declarations just below.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: The Rays' power from unexpected placesRaise your hand if you'd heard of Víctor Mesa Jr. and Ryan Vilade before tonightWhen you think of the 2026 Rays and power, you inevitably think of MVP candidate Junior Caminero, who launched 42 homers during the regular season. Then you probably think of Jonathan Arando and Yandy Díaz, who had 22 apiece.
You might not think of outfielder Víctor Mesa Jr. and utility guy Ryan Vilade, who ranked, respectively, fifth and seventh on the Rays in home runs this season. To be sure, each has some pop, especially Mesa Jr., who batted cleanup in Kevin Cash's Game 3 lineup on Wednesday night. Still, it's fair to call them not the usual suspects when it comes to series-clinching power outbursts. That, though, is precisely what the duo did against the Yankees.First, it was Vilade, who broke a fourth-inning tie by going yard to the opposite field off a 2-1 Max Fried fastball:Statcast estimates that would've been a home run in six of 30 MLB parks, so it wasn't entirely a Yankee Stadium special.
The game was tied again in the top of the sixth when Mesa Jr. bombed a first-pitch sweeper from Fried to deep right center:Mesa knew it, as they say. That made it a 4-2 lead for Tampa Bay, and although the Yankees would draw a run closer it was enough to send the Rays to the ALCS.
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Loser: Anthony Volpe   The fan interference wasn't his fault, but it hurt nonetheless Not because he played poorly. Far from it. Volpe was maybe the best Yankee on the field in Game 3. Either him or Ben Rice. Volpe went 2 for 4 with a run-scoring double in Game 3, but that double is why he's a loser. He's a loser because he "lost" a game-tying two-run homer. Replays showed a fan reached over the left field wall and interfered with the ball, so it was overturned into a double.  
Here's the play. Volpe and everyone in Yankee Stadium thought he hit the game-tying home run. He even got to trot all the way around the bases. The side angle makes it pretty clear though. The ball wasn't going over the wall. From the high of thinking you hit a game-tying homer to the letdown of having to settle for a one-run double. Still productive! Just not quite the same.  "After viewing all relevant angles, the Replay Official definitively determined the spectator interfered with the ball over the field of play," MLB's Replay Center said in a statement. "The ball would not have left the playing field nor would it have been caught. The call is OVERTURNED, there was spectator interference and no home run. Additionally, the Replay Official scored one run and placed the batter-runner at second."  Game 3 was Volpe's only start of the ALDS and his first start since Game 1 of the Wild Card Series against the Red Sox. He went 1 for 3 in that game, so that's 3 for 7 in the postseason. I don't think the Yankees would have won the ALDS had Volpe started Games 1 and 2, but it probably wouldn't have hurt. Fan interference -- correctly called, to be sure -- took away a game-tying homer. That's a tough break with the season on the line.  

                            
    
                                                
                    
      Winner: Andy Pages    One of the Dodgers' worst playoff hitters came through with redemption  Believe it or not, the Dodgers entered Game 4 of the NLDS having only scored runs on home runs thus far in the series. Seven home runs had brought home 10 Dodgers runs, and that was enough to give them a 2-1 lead in the best-of-five series. They had gone 0 for 13 with runners in scoring position.   An error scored them a run early in Game 4, but they still hadn't gotten a clutch hit without muscling up for big-time power.   Fast-forward to the top of the seventh inning. It was a 1-1 game. Braves reliever Didier Fuentes came on with a runner on and two outs. He got a groundout before he walked two Dodgers hitters and manager Walt Weiss decided to turn to the veteran Robert Suarez with the bases loaded and two out. Andy Pages was coming to the plate.   
Pages came through with a line-drive single up the middle to plate two runs.   Not only was it the knock that ended up sending the Dodgers back to the NLCS, but it was a bit of playoff redemption for Pages. He was so bad at the plate last year in the playoffs that the Dodgers elected to remove him from the starting lineup for Games 6 and 7 of the World Series after previously starting him every game. Heading into Game 4 on Wednesday, Pages was a career .123/.165/.210 hitter in the playoffs.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Loser: Braves situational hitting    The Braves went 1 for 23 in the series with RISP  Thanks particularly to five walks issued by Dodgers starting pitcher Tyler Glasnow, the Braves had their share of chances to score runs in Game 4. They just couldn't come through in the clutch the way Pages did for the Dodgers. Well, that and they also had some rough batted-ball luck.   A leadoff Ozzie Albies double in the sixth inning didn't amount to any runs. Per Statcast, that double, by the way, would've been a home run in 29 of the 30 MLB ballparks. It's just that they happened to be playing in the one where it didn't leave the yard. Then Mauricio Dubón sent a two-out liner to right field that hung up just long enough for Kyle Tucker to catch it. The expected batting average there was .620.   
They also failed, though. Plenty in the entire series. In Game 1, they were 0 for 4 with runners in scoring position. In Game 2, despite the win, the Braves left 11 men on base. In Game 3, they were 0 for 6 with runners in scoring position, leaving six more on base.   In Game 4? Yep, that would be 0 for 7 with seven left on.  In all, that's 1 for 23 with runners in scoring position in the four-game series with 28 runners left on.   Part of this is a function of facing great playoff pitching against a defense that is always very well-positioned. Part of it is simply bad luck in where the balls are hit hard. Part of it is a failure in execution.   
Taking splits like RISP stats isn't a predictive measure or anything like that, but it can tell the story in a series like this. In the case of the Dodgers taking the Braves out, we got here in large part due to the Braves leaving a high school classroom's worth of runners on base.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Winner: Jo Adell    The Guardians acquired Adell in front of the trade deadline and he's been an RBI machine  As the trade deadline came into focus, the Guardians, looking for cheap help on offense, ended up grabbing outfielder Jo Adell from the Angels in exchange for Double-A catcher Jacob Cozart. In 48 games for Cleveland, Adell posted a 108 OPS+ and drove home 32 runs. In Game 2, he recorded an eighth-inning RBI triple that nearly left the yard.  In Game 3 on Wednesday in Game 3, he came to the plate with two outs, bases loaded and a tied 1-1 score. Adell came through in a big way.   
Just like that, it was a 4-1 Guardians lead. Adell also became the 16th player in postseason history to triple in back-to-back games (via Sarah Langs).   Adell's three-RBI triple moved the Guardians' chances to win the game from 52.8% to 78.8%. This was the largest difference-maker in the game, and a monster shift at that.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Loser: White Sox's missed opportunities    The White Sox had plenty of chances for crooked numbers in this one  Playing in front of an electric crowd, ready to clinch a postseason series at home for the first time since 1906 (and we all remember that one, right?), the White Sox had several chances to put up a crooked number and weren't able to come through.   
In the first, Sam Anonacci walked and Miguel Vargas singled to give them two runners with no outs. Kyle Teel came through with a one-out double, but Vargas was held at third. Chase Meidroth and Tristan Peters struck out to leave two on base.Meidroth and Peters started the fourth with consecutive doubles, but the following three hitters were retired, so, again, the White Sox settled for just the one run.In the fifth, Antonacci singled and Vargas walked. The runners moved up on a grounder and then Teel ripped a line drive toward right field, only to watch it get snared by Guardians second baseman Travis Bazzana, who then doubled Vargas off second. The expected batting average on this one makes it even tougher to swallow for the White Sox faithful, as it was .940. This means that 94% of the time a ball hit with that exit velocity at that launch angle ends up as a hit. This was one of the 6% that found a glove. In the sixth, with two outs, Braden Montgomery walked, Randal Grichuk singled, Colson Montgomery was hit by a pitch and then so was Antonacci. They got a run, but the bases were loaded for their best player, Vargas. He hit a rocket toward left, but Guardians third baseman José Ramírez was able to knock the ball down and get Vargas at first. Vargas hit it hard, with a .580 expected batting average. It just didn't work out. You never want to come away empty-handed in those innings, and the White Sox were able to get a single run in three of those frames. Still, it feels like there was a lot left on the board here from the home team. An explosion in a single inning could've demoralized the Guardians and ultimately sent them home. Some of the issues were their own fault, and some were bad luck. It all added up to a Game 4 White Sox loss.

title: Change in Houston: DeMeco Ryans taking over defensive play-calling duties from Matt Burke - CBS Sports

        On Wednesday, Houston Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said he will take over defensive play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Matt Burke, a significant change amid his team's 0-4 start."It all starts with me," Ryans said. "If there's a lack in communication, I look at myself first, so it starts with me and making sure I'm a better communicator, so just to help spark things more, I'm gonna take over the play calling for the defense, and I'm gonna make sure the communication is right. If our guys are saying the communication is not right, then ... ultimately it falls on me. So it's on me to get it fixed."It's no slight against coach Burke. He's done an outstanding job. Just wanna make sure I can streamline communication in the best way possible, so that isn't the theme when I stand up here the next time I see you guys and talking about communication."The change comes on the heels of Houston's 34-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys in which Dallas racked up 399 yards of offense and scored touchdowns on four of its five second-half drives. CeeDee Lamb had 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown, and Dak Prescott threw for 335 yards. Dallas did not have a single turnover.It was the second time in four weeks that the defense was not up to its usual excellent standard. The Bills beat the Texans 36-31 in Week 1. Houston still ranks highly in many categories, but one notable drop-off has been in the number of big plays it is giving up.
Texans' defensive ranks20252026Success rate2nd8thSack rate8th3rdNet yards per attempt4th25thExplosive play rate14th28thThe Texans' defense gives up some big plays by nature -- it is an extremely aggressive unit that will sometimes get beaten -- but the fall from 14th to 28th in explosive play rate is massive. Several big plays have also come in crucial moments, magnifying the problem even more.In Week 1, Josh Allen threw a game-winning 34-yard touchdown pass to Joshua Palmer with under a minute left.In Week 3, Daniel Jones found Laquon Treadwell for 20 yards with under two minutes left before the game-winning field goal.In Week 4, Prescott found George Pickens for 22 yards with under a minute left shortly before the game-winning touchdown.The Texans have allowed 17 completions of 20+ yards. Only the Lions have allowed more. There is much more to "communication" than just defending big plays -- many of those completions were well-defended -- but that is one area in which Houston is lacking.Last year, Ryans gave up play-calling duties to Burke in Week 4, ironically, after the Texans' defense had been struggling early. Ryans is now hoping the inverse decision from last year will provide a similar spark.
The Texans started 1-3 last season and made the playoffs. Only one team -- the 1992 Chargers -- started a season 0-4 and made the postseason. The Texans will hope their march to join them starts with a win in Week 5 at the Titans.

title: Mike Breen apologizes after LeBron James refutes story alleging he called out Joel Embiid - CBS Sports
description: Breen apologized for causing a stir with an anecdote he shared while calling a preseason Knicks-Sixers game
body:
Breen apologized for causing a stir with an anecdote he shared while calling a preseason Knicks-Sixers game

    6:30 pm ET

        The Philadelphia 76ers are going to be under a microscope all season after making two massive roster moves this summer by trading for Jaylen Brown and signing LeBron James to create a star-studded starting lineup. There is no shortage of intrigue about how this group will pan out and how all the various egos and personalities will mesh on and off the court. Everyone wants a peek behind the curtain at how this new experiment is going, and during the MSG broadcast of Monday night's preseason opener between the Knicks and Sixers, Mike Breen, New York's longtime play-by-play announcer, offered what he thought was a harmless anecdote about James' leadership already being on display. "Somebody told me before the game that they were out ready to practice, and Joel Embiid walked out on the court a couple of minutes late, and LeBron let him hear it," Breen said on the air. What Breen failed to consider in the moment is that Embiid, who has a history of reported tardiness, being the other player in the story made the story go viral and eventually James took to Instagram to deny it happened, insisting Embiid "ain't been late so stop the lies." 

        
            
                Eight pressing NBA questions for 2026-27 season: Will Knicks repeat? Can 76ers finally break through?
                
                    John Gonzalez                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Whether the anecdote Breen had been told and repeated on air was true or not, James knows how delicate the situation is right now and wanted to nip any questions about Embiid's professionalism in the bud to avoid it becoming a topic before the season even started. Breen spoke with ESPN to apologize for starting an entire news cycle with his comments, and noted that while he was told the information by someone he trusts, if James says it didn't happen, he believes him. "I don't know why the person who told me the story would make it up, but if LeBron says it never happened then I believe him and apologize for putting it out there," Breen said. 
He also felt bad about not recognizing that simply by stating it was Embiid, the story would get legs and become much bigger than an announcer trying to fill time and offer a tidbit of information during a preseason broadcast. "For me, the fact that the teammate was Joel was meaningless. In hindsight, I should have realized the fact that it was Joel is what made it a story," Breen said. "I've always been a huge fan of Joel and feel awful that it put the focus on him the way that it did."That it took just one preseason game for this kind of silly controversy to arise is a precursor to what is to come all year for the Sixers. The good, the bad and the mundane will all be amplified, and while all parties involved seem ready to sweep this story away, there will be plenty more to come.

Miller imploded in Game 2 of the NLDS against the Brewers, then went on the paternity list and missed Game 3

        Padres closer Mason Miller is back and good to go for Game 4 in San Diego on Wednesday night as his team tries to stave off elimination again. He was reactivated for the game and Wandy Rodriguez was removed, the team announced Wednesday afternoon.Miller was placed on the paternity list prior to Game 3 of the NLDS with the Padres trailing the Brewers 0-2 in the best-of-five series. The Padres were able to pull off the victory in Game 3 with a 4-3 win, which included a two-inning save by starting pitcher Michael King.In Sunday's Game 2, with the Padres clinging to a one-run lead late, Miller failed to pull off his own two-inning save. Instead, the Brewers stormed back and won in walk-off fashion to take the 2-0 series lead. Miller recorded outs vs. the first four hitters he faced, but then walked three of the next four hitters he saw and gave up a two-RBI single to Jackson Chourio to take the blown save and loss. Entering Game 4, Miller is now on three days of rest. He came into the playoffs as arguably the best closer in baseball, racking up 38 saves and a 1.67 ERA in the regular season.
Meanwhile, lefty Adrián Morejón, the Padres' second-biggest late-inning gun, hasn't pitched since going two innings in Game 1. It made sense that he didn't pitch in Game 2, but he wasn't available in Game 3 either, due to a previously undisclosed shoulder issue. Stammen said on Wednesday that he's "hopeful" Morejón will be available."Still feeling a little stickiness in the shoulder," Stammen said after Game 3. "We're trying to work through it. We're doing everything we can to get him ready. We'll see his status about tomorrow, but he was definitely feeling a little bit better today but just didn't feel like he could go."There's definitely a chance [he pitches in Game 4], yeah. We'll see. We've got to evaluate him [Wednesday] like we did today and put him in a safe space to be able to pitch. We don't want to put him out there if he's compromised."
The Padres still have excellent relievers like Jason Adam and Bradgley Rodriguez, but the bullpen is a monster force when the best versions of Miller and Morejón are 100%. Perhaps we'll find out in Game 4 if that's the case.

title: South Carolina's Dylan Stewart on track to play vs. Florida after one-game suspension - CBS Sports
description: Stewart was suspended for one game by the SEC and 'indefinitely' by coach Shane Beamer after punching an Alabama
body:
Stewart was suspended for one game by the SEC and 'indefinitely' by coach Shane Beamer after punching an Alabama player on Sept. 26
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Oct 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        South Carolina EDGE Dylan Stewart is on track to play this Saturday if things continue to progress in the correct direction, CBS Sports' Chris Hummer and Matt Zenitz report.Stewart returned to team activities on Monday after serving a one-game suspension from the SEC for striking an Alabama player in the Gamecocks' loss to the Crimson Tide. In addition to punishment from the conference, Stewart is currently on an indefinite suspension from Beamer. "He came back today and was in the 8 a.m. team meeting we had this morning, and he was at practice," Beamer said. "As I've told him and the team, his status will be determined as we go throughout the week."Stewart was a five-star recruit in the Class of 2024 and one of the most significant recruits of the Beamer era at South Carolina. The junior posted a combined 22.5 tackles for loss and 11 sacks in his first two seasons with the program.
He has yet to record a sack over two games as he works his way back from injury."I do believe my job as the head coach is to win football games, but it's also to help young men and help them grow," Beamer said. "Last week was a learning lesson from him and I (hope) there was growth from that. He's a good young man that I care a lot about. He's not, and I'm not condoning his actions in Tuscaloosa at all, and it's unacceptable, but he's not the first person that has ever punched a player in a game, and he won't be the last."Beamer on the hot seatStewart's return would be a big on-field boost for a South Carolina team in desperate need of one. Beamer entered the season on the hot seat, and that temperature has only increased after three straight losses. Last week's 35-34 overtime defeat to Kentucky was the team's eighth straight in the SEC and 12th setback in its last 14 games against Power Four opponents.Few coaches are facing the amount of pressure that Beamer's under right now, but he doesn't seem worried about his status heading into a Week 6 showdown at Florida.
"It's a challenge. It is what it is. It's week to week in this league and I know that. Right now, 2-3 is not good enough," Beamer said Tuesday. "I haven't been good enough as a head coach. I own it. We've got to get better as a football team. It really doesn't change, going into it versus in it. Right now, I'm focusing on what I can control, and that's trying to put together the best team to go play on Saturdays to give us the best chance to be successful on Saturdays."All I can go on is the conversations I've had with (athletic director) Jeremiah (Donati), (senior deputy director of athletics) Jeff Crane, and the text message I got from our president emeritus over the weekend -- who's been awesome. Some of our biggest donors that I've gotten phone calls, voicemails and text messages … that's why I go on, not what people and their 'sources' say. Then it doesn't happen, and suddenly it's, 'well, my sources now say this. "It's like c'mon man."Recent social media comments about his job on a post centered on his daughter's senior night at her high school, the night before South Carolina's loss to Mississippi State, really bothered Beamer.
"There's some crappy people in the world, there just is," Beamer said, who is currently on a three-week break from checking his phone, he confirmed.CBS Sports reported on Monday that Beamer's job security isn't as tenuous as it seems due to financial constraints at the university.Beamer has mentioned the support he has from the school's administration several times during this current three-game slide and said as much during Tuesday's press conference.
"I don't know if social media is always real-life," Beamer said. "What you see on social media vs. what is actually real. I know the noise out there last week versus what was actually real."The same people in the student section against Mississippi State, chanting 'Fire Beamer' at the end of the game, seven days earlier, they were screaming 'Beamer Ball' at the end of the game when we beat Towson. It's truly week to week."

title: BYU RB LJ Martin to miss a month with injury, including Oct. 17 game vs. Notre Dame - CBS Sports
description: The Cougars will be without their star running back in an Oct. 17 top-10 showdown against Notre Dame
body:
The Cougars will be without their star running back in an Oct. 17 top-10 showdown against Notre Dame
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:49 pm ET

        The BYU offense just absorbed a big blow weeks before its highly anticipated showdown with Notre Dame. Star running back and 2025 Big 12 Player of the Year LJ Martin will be out for at least one month due to a lower-body injury, ESPN reports.Martin carried the ball just twice for 16 yards in last week's win over TCU before exiting the game. With 4:40 remaining in the first quarter, Martin was pulled down awkwardly, jogged off the field with a slight limp and did not return.With Martin out of the game, the Cougars were without their top two running backs since Sione Moa has been sidelined with an injury he suffered in Week 1. As a result, the BYU rushing attack wasn't nearly as effective as it usually is. The Cougars rushed for just 154 yards and 4.1 yards per carry in wet conditions.Prior to the injury, Martin was a key cog in the BYU offense, as usual. Through the first three games, Martin rushed the ball 42 times for 328 yards and three touchdowns. He was also involved in the passing game with five receptions for 41 yards.
In his career, Martin has piled up 2,885 rushing yards, 439 receiving yards and 29 total touchdowns. He'll be a hard weapon to replace.The timeline for Martin's return means he'll miss the Oct. 17 showdown against Notre Dame, which will be critical for the College Football Playoff hopes of both teams. With Martin on the shelf for that one, BYU either needs someone else to step up on the ground, or it needs to find more production from its passing game.BYU's air attack has been groundedA lack of depth at running back isn't ideal for BYU, a team that thrives when it runs the ball effectively. The Cougars rank 16th nationally and fourth in the Big 12 with 235.5 rushing yards per game.
Martin has been a big part of that -- his 344 rushing yards lead the team -- but so has quarterback Bear Bachmeier. The sophomore signal caller has rushed for 130 yards, and he's been particularly effective down near the goal line. Bachmeier was first on the team with four rushing scores.The issue for Bachmeier and the Cougars is that the passing game hasn't quite clicked. Bachmeier has completed 64.9 percent of his passes for just 704 yards, seven touchdowns and one interception. BYU's 179.8 passing yards per game rank 114th nationally.The lack of a cohesive passing game isn't exactly a shock. The Cougars' top three receivers from last season are no longer on the team, and although freshman Legend Glasker has been great, that production hasn't been fully replaced.
If BYU is going to navigate the next month without Martin, it will have to figure some things out in the passing game, especially against the Fighting Irish. Notre Dame's defense will have a field day if the Cougars are one-dimensional.

body:
Moore is expected to miss Saturday's Big Ten game against UCLA, leaving Dylan Raiola as the likely starter against the Bruins

        Oregon quarterback Dante Moore has been ruled out for the Ducks game against UCLA, the team announced in its injury report on Wednesday evening.Moore suffered the concussion on Sept. 26 when he gave himself up in the second quarter on a slide and took a shot to the helmet from USC linebacker Desman Stephens II, who was suspended for the tackle.Oregon coach Dan Lanning said last Saturday on "Big Noon Kickoff" that the program is exercising an "abundance of caution" and there's no timetable for his return, emphasizing there is no rush in his recovery. "Similar to what we said before, we're gonna do what's best for Dante moving forward," Lanning reiterated in his Monday press conference. "It was great to see him back out there with his teammates getting to work today."
If Moore is unable to play against the Bruins, backup quarterback and offseason Nebraska transfer Dylan Raiola will be making his first start for the Ducks after coming off the bench to lead the win over USC.Raiola led four touchdown drives in the second half, including a pair of decisive scores in the fourth quarter to break open the game on the road."I'm just so proud of him," Lanning said of Raiola. "You talk about owning a role and not waiting for your opportunity but preparing for your opportunity, and Dylan's a guy that prepared for his opportunity."
Oregon's Big Ten, CFP predicamentThis would be a much easier decision on Oregon's coaching staff is the Ducks were unbeaten right now and had the luxury of easing Moore back into the starting lineup while also seeing what Raiola could do in full operation of the first-team offense. Instead, a loss to UCLA further clouds the conference championship picture and puts Oregon in must-win mode the rest of the way in terms of reaching the College Football Playoff.Oregon is projected to reach the 12-team bracket in our latest projection at CBS Sports as the league's third and final selection, but the Ducks still have to play Ohio State and Washington down the stretch following Saturday's showdown with UCLA.
There's a home bout with Nebraska next week as well, and the Huskers are 5-0 this season with seventh-ranked Indiana coming into Lincoln this weekend. Northwestern and Michigan are other conference games that, while the Ducks are favored to win, could give them trouble.Moore's return timelineAccording to the NCAA's concussion protocol safety checklist, all athletes who have suffered a concussion must undergo a pre-participation baseline assessment, which includes a documented history of injuries, a symptom evaluation and cognitive and balance tests to establish a comparison point.
The team physician determines "pre-participation clearance and/or the need for additional consultation or testing." The NCAA mandates that when an athlete shows signs of a concussion, they are not allowed to return to the game.The NCAA's concussion safety protocol management guidelines state that a player's return to play is a step-by-step process that must be completed without symptoms returning -- almost like weather delays, when a single streak of lightning in the area delays a return to action.The five stages of an athlete's return to play via the NCAA are as follows:Stage 1: Symptom-limited activity: Begin with light aerobic exercise.Stage 2: Moderate aerobic exercise: Increase the intensity of the aerobic exercise.Stage 3: Non-contact drills: Introduce sport-specific drills in full uniform without physical contact.Stage 4: Full-contact practice: Allow full-contact practice or training.Stage 5: Return to competition: An athlete can return to game play only after successfully completing all prior stages and receiving medical clearance.With Monday's return to practice, the next update from Lanning and the Ducks' coaching staff on Moore comes later this week.
Uncomfortable decision loomingGiven Moore's status and Raiola's play off the bench, Lanning has a difficult choice on who to play in the coming weeks if his starter is ready to return to action.Raiola completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, executing Oregon's offense to near perfection in the second half of the win over the Trojans. This comes after the Ducks had looked out of rhythm several times in the early going this fall, following a near-stumble against Boise State and a loss at Oklahoma State.Moore has thrown for 926 yards and nine touchdowns without an interception through four games, but four of those scores came during an 84-0 win over Portland State -- a glorified practice for the Ducks following two shaky performances during the first two weeks.
Oregon hasn't yet hit its stride offensively with its senior, returning star at quarterback, but it closely resembled the team that was clicking on all cylinders and reached the CFP last season with Raiola back there in Los Angeles.

Sources tell CBS Sports the Ducks will likely roll with Raiola against the Bruins as Moore continues his recovery from a concussion
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:14 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Despite returning to practice this week, Oregon quarterback Dante Moore has been ruled out for his team's top-25 matchup against UCLA on Saturday, per the Wednesday night availability report. Earlier in the day, sources told CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz that Moore was unlikely to play in Week 6.On Monday, Ducks coach Dan Lanning said that Moore was back at practice in shoulder pads and a helmet, but the team is taking things slowly with its star quarterback. "Dante was out there at practice for us today," Lanning said at his weekly press conference. "Similar to what we said before, we're gonna do what's best for Dante moving forward. ... It was great to see him back out there with his teammates getting to work today."Moore has been recovering from a concussion since taking a dangerous hit to the head against USC on Sept. 26. Trojans linebacker Desman Stephens Jr. struck a forceful blow to Moore's head as he was sliding, and the Oregon quarterback had to be stretchered off the field.
The NCAA's return-to-play protocol for players in the concussion protocol features five stages.Stage 1: Symptom-limited activity: Begin with light aerobic exercise.Stage 2: Moderate aerobic exercise: Increase the intensity of the aerobic exercise.Stage 3: Non-contact drills: Introduce sport-specific drills in full uniform without physical contact.Stage 4: Full-contact practice: Allow full-contact practice or training.Stage 5: Return to competition: An athlete can return to game play only after successfully completing all prior stages and receiving medical clearance.Given that Moore is back at practice, it would be fair to assume he's at least reached Stage 3, but how his body responds to ramping up at practice will be critical for his return timeline.This news means backup Dylan Raiola will likely get his first start at Oregon against UCLA. A former five-star recruit, Raiola transferred from Nebraska in the offseason, and his willingness to play the role of backup for one season is already benefiting him and the Ducks.
In relief of Moore, Raiola torched the USC secondary for 289 yards and a pair of touchdowns. He may need a similar effort this weekend as Oregon faces a UCLA team that has been lighting up the scoreboard under first-year coach Bob Chesney.Confidence in RaiolaRaiola played extremely well in relief of Moore a couple of weeks ago, but it will be his show from the first snap of the game on Saturday. Does being the starter require a shift in mindset for Raiola? Lanning doesn't think so."No, there isn't a shift," Lanning said on Monday. "If he can just play like he played last time every single time, I think we'd be sitting in a really good situation. Dylan's got to keep doing what he's been doing, preparing like he's going to be the guy who goes out there every single day. We need that from every single person on our team. We don't need anything special from Dylan other than doing what he's been doing."
Lanning added that Raiola has shown tremendous accuracy on the practice field, and that showed up on the field against the Trojans. If that keeps up, the Ducks' offense should be just fine."I think all those things show up," Lanning said. "He can play quarterback at a high level. I think he showed his accuracy in this last game and his decision-making. That's shown up for him, and it's shown up for him in practice. Again, I would just ask him to keep doing the same things he's been doing in practice."Among backup quarterbacks around the country, Raiola has a strong case for being the best. How many teams can bring in a player with 24 games of experience, 5,232 passing yards and 36 touchdowns off the bench?
Raiola shouldn't be shaken by the moment in a key top-25 matchup on Saturday afternoon (3:30 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+Premium).

body:
Pochettino used the first post-World Cup international break to hand 13 different players their first cap, overseeing a generational shift as the road to the 2030 World Cup begins
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:37 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It is difficult to fight the post-World Cup lull; the quick transition out of sports' most anticipated event is hard to avoid. The U.S. men's national team have managed to buck the trend at the start of a new four-year cycle, though, thanks to the introduction of a baker's dozen of fresh faces eager to make their opportunities count with the 2030 World Cup in mind.Head coach Mauricio Pochettino embarked on his most future-focused player pool expansion project yet, mixing a group of newcomers with an average age of 19 years old with several World Cup participants as he oversees a generational shift. The results have spoken for themselves so far – the USMNT went four for four in their fall friendlies, a selection of young players impressing nearly every step of the way as the likes of Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada threw different challenges at them. The head coach has been effusive with his praise of the newcomers for being eager to learn and showcase their talents, while also showering his veterans with compliments for their welcoming nature.He has refused to single players out, especially the first-timers, championing the collective at this early juncture of the cycle. Take, for example, his response to a question about Cavan Sullivan after the 17-year-old scored his first international goal in a 3-0 win over Mexico on Saturday. He complimented Sullivan – and the rest of the group "like Mathis [Albert], like Justin [Ellis], like Julian [Hall], like Frankie [Westfield], like Neil [Pierre], like Brooklyn [Raines], like Adri [Mehmeti], like Peyton [Miller], like Cole [Campbell] … [Did] I miss some young [players]? Gozo, Zavier Gozo."Even as Pochettino retained a focus on the group from start to finish this fall, some inevitably rose above the rest. The head coach has held his cards close to his chest in a variety of ways over the course of the four-game swing, only hinting at the squad turnover that awaits over the next four years. The goalkeeper situation, for example, is something to keep an eye on – Diego Kochen and Brian Schwake played 135 minutes each, more than the other two shot-stoppers in camp who just so happened to be on this year's World Cup roster, Matt Freese and Chris Brady. To say that is a clear indication of Pochettino's plans for the future would be a bridge too far but even as he cloaks his answers, some appear more obvious than others.
Much will be revealed with his roster for November's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti, for which Pochettino is expected to call in a full-strength version of the team. What exactly that looks like right now, though, is the big question – and a few of the USMNT's newcomers might be ready to answer it.Julian Hall, Justin Ellis take top marksThe winner of the window is unquestionably Julian Hall, who scored three goals and notched one assist in his first four caps and earned more playing time than his fellow newcomers with 52.25 average minutes per game. Hall snapped a 12-game goalless run just in time for his first reps with the senior national team and has been on a roll ever since, his natural striker's instincts ensuring he would score against Chile and Mexico despite uneven team performances and his own room for improvement. The 18-year-old could still be a lot quicker when it comes to making decisions and can go under the radar in games but those feel like teachable skills for a player who is still in the very early stages of his career. He seems to have Pochettino's admiration, even if the coach will not come out and say it just yet. Hall's minutes tally is likely padded by Ellis' injury on Tuesday, but he won the wide-open race to start against Mexico and come on against Canada despite Damion Downs being available.Ellis also deserves praise for his two goals this window, his playing time perhaps cut short by the injury he sustained in Tuesday's 1-0 win over Canada that forced a halftime substitution. Ellis has a talent for shot creation that makes him a different type of forward than Hall but an equally useful one, though he did spend the last week and change showing off his ability to score. Both have a reasonable argument to return to the fold as soon as November, especially since the USMNT are not particularly deep there. World Cup goalscorer Folarin Balogun is building match fitness after missing the beginning of the season with Monaco, while Ricardo Pepi withdrew from the fall friendlies with an injury of his own. Pochettino had always planned to evaluate both Hall and Ellis, each of them passing the early tests of their USMNT careers.
"We were sad because of the injury of Ricardo but in football [or] soccer, always when something not good happens, it's an opportunity for another but they need to be ready to take the possibility," Pochettino said Tuesday. "The plan was already [there] with Justin and Julian, give the possibility to play even with Ricardo [in] the camp, like you saw with the 'keepers."Cavan Sullivan's strong first steps into the limelightIf there is anyone in particular Pochettino seems to be protecting, it's Sullivan. The 17-year-old is already the face of the USMNT's next generation and the head coach has not exactly shied away from that, to the point that Sullivan started against Mexico and averaged 33.5 minutes per game this window, slightly more than Ellis did. Pochettino's management of Sullivan, though, feels like an example in being patient with a player for whom the sky is the limit.He fielded more questions about Sullivan than any other player this fall and was slow to offer specific praise for him in a way he often is not with more experienced players. Pochettino appeared to take a balanced and subtle approach in press conferences because he recognizes the teenager's potential, not in spite of it. That was apparent in his roster selection, too – Sullivan benefitted from not having to carry the spotlight or the load by himself, a healthy number of newcomers undergoing the same journey with him and several veterans around to show them the way. Pochettino used questions about Sullivan to lay out his non-negotiables because he is the player with the attention focused squarely on him, and therefore the perfect hook by which to set an example for the rest of the group. Pochettino's examples are always laced with compliments, though, which eventually sneak out of him when he runs out of cautious optimism.
"He's a talented player with enormous quality but with a very good balance in possession and out of possession," Pochettino said after the win over Mexico. "He's a fighter. He's a warrior. It's difficult to find these types of players with tremendous quality with the ball in possession. I think Cavan enjoys, in possession with the ball [at] the feet like when he needs to [be] chasing people and recover the ball, no? That is my impression after nearly three weeks together and that is unbelievable, to have a player like this. I think it's fantastic news for USA … Happy for him, happy for the team. I like what he said after the game: the most important [thing] was the result. Learning every day, that is the good thing."Brooklyn Raines fills a position of needMidfielder Brooklyn Raines has quietly had a solid window, ranking second of the newcomers with an average of 43 minutes per game but then again, defensive midfielders tend to go under the radar. He will be someone to keep an eye on in the short term because he enters the player pool in a position of need – the USMNT went to the World Cup without a true back-up for Tyler Adams, a decision partly influenced by injuries and partly down to player selection. No one has become Adams' clear back-up since the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and it is entirely possible Pochettino will be slow to decide who might be the captain's understudy – he does have time on the clock, after all. Still, his reliance on Raines in the fall friendlies is a signal that the 21-year-old has a chance to stake his claim.Gio Reyna, a newfound leaderThe newcomers were well-positioned to make headlines during the fall friendlies and did just that but joining them were an eclectic mix of experienced players, all of whom were tasked with being role models to their younger teammates and showing them the ropes. A batch of these selections made perfect sense – Adams and Chris Richards had emerged as leaders within the group years ago, while Sebastian Berhalter always seemed to boast the mentality to join the ranks. Pochettino's praise for the veterans was not unwarranted because over the course of the international break, they all seemed to adjust to their responsibilities well, even if someone like Alex Freeman is not that much older than the fresh faces. One person really seemed to rise to the challenge – Gio Reyna.
Christian Pulisic has been the face of the USMNT for a decade now but Reyna was always the most naturally gifted player of his generation, his potential still a leading narrative even at the age of 24. He has not had it easy since making his professional debut in 2020, injuries and a lack of playing time at the club level hindering his progress. How exactly he would transition from being the next big thing to welcoming a whole group of them was a fascinating question, but Reyna has relished the role of mentor. Like the leaders that came before him, Reyna is beginning to position himself as a conduit between the coaching staff and the newer players."I think all camp, we've had a very consistent message," he said after the Mexico win. "These games obviously are non-official games but we're not treating them different than any sort of official games, whether it's a qualifying game or a World Cup game or Gold Cup, whatever it is. Our goal is to win every game and so far, we're doing well and today was a very good win against a very good team and we knew it wasn't going to be easy but we dug deep. Credit to the guys for a really well-rounded team performance."It also helps that things are finally coming up Reyna – he now has eight consecutive starts for club and country, the first time he's managed that streak in his entire career. The skill he's obviously possessed for the better part of a decade is becoming easier to see, too.
"I think it's a good thing that he starts to play the season with Strasbourg and that makes [it] easier, after, to adapt here with the national team and I think to have the continuity in his club helps us a lot," Pochettino said after the win against Canada. "He's a player that we were talking [has] the capacity, the understanding of the game. He's a player that can play in different positions [on] the pitch and I think the quality he has matches what we expect from our team, for the players on the field. That question also with Malik, it's really well because they can swap the positions, they have a very good creative mind. Yes, I think Gio is really mature now. He's still so young but he's one of the leaders of the group, too and he's helping a lot, always positive. All the things that we were seeing [in] him are all so positive. It's why we trust [in] him playing."

The early NFL season has been dominated by high-profile injuries, and if anything, that unfortunate trend only picked up in Week 4. Lamar Jackson, Ja'Marr Chase, Saquon Barkley, Tee Higgins and Rashee Rice were just a few of the big names to leave their respective contests early, and that's only on the offensive side of the ball.Quarterback has been especially hard-hit this season, with Jaxson Dart done for the season and Jackson, Jayden Daniels, Caleb Williams, Baker Mayfield, Sam Darnold, Kyler Murray have all missed time with injuries suffered this season. Health can be one of the biggest factors, especially as injuries pile up throughout the rugged 17-game, 18-week schedule.Two teams -- the Chiefs and the Panthers -- get their bye and a chance to heal up in Week 5, and the Rams face the Bills on "Monday Night Football," so they're not practicing Wednesday. As such, we're taking a look at the initial injury reports for the 28 teams playing on Thursday and Sunday.Odds courtesy of DraftKings SportsbookTampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5)Buccaneers: QB Baker Mayfield (thumb), LB SirVocea Dennis (ankle, foot), CB Benjamin Morrison (quad), S Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) OUTCowboys: CB Cobie Durant (hamstring), LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), T Drew Shelton (hamstring) OUT; G Tyler Smith (thumb), WR Jonathan Mingo (illness) QUESTIONABLENot only are the Buccaneers down their starting quarterback -- they'll turn to Jalon Daniels for the second straight week -- but they're down two key members of their secondary, too, against one of the league's best passing attacks. Morrison got hurt early in Week 3 and hasn't played since, and Winfield fractured a rib in Week 4. In better news, Rueben Bain Jr. (groin, shoulder) carries no injury designation into the game after missing Week 4.
The Cowboys are dealing with plenty of defensive injuries as well, but the most noteworthy development is the potential season debut of Tyler Smith, the team's top offensive lineman. He's officially questionable.Philadelphia Eagles at Jacksonville Jaguars (-7) in LondonSeveral notable Eagles, including RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring), LB Jihaad Campbell (knee) and OLB Jonathan Greenard (ankle), did not participate Wednesday. WR Marquise Browns (ankle), S Marcus Epps (groin) and C/G Drew Kendall also didn't practice. LB Zack Baun (concussion), TE Dallas Goedert (knee), T Fred Johnson (knee) and CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) were limited.S Eric Murray (concussion) was the only Jaguars player not practicing. CB Montaric Brown (hamstring), DT DaVon Hamilton (foot), T Anton Harrison (elbow), DE Josh Hines-Allen (groin), CB Jarrian Jones (foot), CB Jourdan Lewis (hamstring) and G Cole Van Lanen (knee) were all limited.
Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers (-2.5)The Bears were again without QB Caleb Williams (hamstring), who hasn't played since Week 2. Their top two running backs Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) and RB D'Andre Swift also didn't practice Wednesday, and neither did OL Jonah Jackson (ankle), DL Grady Jarrett (NRI/rest), OL Joe Thuney (pec) and OL Darnell Wright (ankle). LB Keyshaun Elliott (quad), LB Noah Sewell (Achilles) and DL Shemar Turner (knee) were limited.For Green Bay, G Aaron Banks (knee, toe), RB Chris Brooks (ankle), G Jager Burton (back) and G Jacob Monk (quad) did not practice. T Anthony Belton (knee), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), LB Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), WR Savion Williams (ankle) and DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle) were limited.Houston Texans (-7.5) at Tennessee TitansDE Will Anderson Jr. (ankle), T Trent Brown (NIR/rest) and LB Jamal Hill (knee) did not practice Wednesday for the Texans. LB Azeez Al-Shaair (groin), DE Jadeveon Clowney (knee), WR Nico Collins (NIR/rest), WR Tank Dell (knee), DE Logan Hall (knee), DT Kayden McDonald (ankle) and T Braden Smith (foot) were all limited. Dell, McDonald and Smith all had their practice windows opened.
For the Titans, DT Jeffery Simmons (back), DL John Franklin-Myers (back), RB Tony Pollard (foot), S Amani Hooker (concussion) and CB Marcus Harris (knee, ankle) did not practice. S Kevin Winston Jr. (shoulder) was limited.Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Miami DolphinsNeither of the Bengals' top wide receivers -- Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) nor Tee Higgins (groin, neck) -- practiced Wednesday. Also not practicing were DT Jonathan Allen (NIR/rest, knee), LB Swayze Bozeman (groin), S Bryan Cook (ankle), S Kyle Dugger (quad). DT Dexter Lawrence (wrist), S Jordan Battle (hamstring), LB Barrett Carter (ankle), G Dalton Risner (knee) and WR Colbie Young (knee) were all limited.Four Dolphins did not practice Wednesday: DE Rob Beal Jr. (hamstring), WR Caleb Douglas (ankle), DB Reese Taylor (quad) and LB Jackson Woodard (ankle). The limited participants were LS Tucker Addington (shoulder), WR Chris Bell (knee), CB Julius Brents (heel), DT Kenneth Grant (toe), T Austin Jackson (knee) and S Dante Trader Jr. (shin).
Las Vegas Raiders at New England Patriots (-3.5)The Raiders were without WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) at Wednesday's practice. TE Brock Bowers (knee), G Spencer Burford (knee), DT Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder), G Jackson Powers-Johnson (groin), WR Cody White (ankle) and G Trey Zuhn III (knee) were all limited. RB Ashton Jeanty (ankle) was a full participant.CB Carlton Davis (neck), CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), WR Mack Hollins (calf) and CB Karon Prunty (hamstring) did not practice for the Patriots on Wednesday. RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), DT Christian Barmore (shoulder), LB Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder), T Morgan Moses (foot), CB Channing Canada (hamstring), LB Christian Elliss (chest), FB Reggie Gilliam (ankle, knee), CB Charles Woods (shoulder) and S Craig Woodson (shoulder) were all limited participants. Drake Maye was listed with a right shoulder injury but was a full participant, as he was for all of last week.Minnesota Vikings (-1.5) at New Orleans SaintsWR Jordan Addison (hamstring), T Christian Darrisaw (concussion) and CB Chuck Demmings (hamstring) were all non-participants for the Vikings' Wednesday practice, while WR Justin Jefferson (ankle), RB Aaron Jones Sr. (NIR/rest) and OT Brian O'Neill (knee) were all limited.
For the Saints, WR Barion Brown (thigh), LB Kaden Elliss (calf), EDGE Anfernee Jennings (knee), RB Alvin Kamara (back) and WR Chris Olave (NIR/rest) were wre listed as non-participants. QB Tyler Shough (left hand), S Julian Blackmon (shoulder), TE Noah Fant (abdomen), EDGE Carl Granderson (ankle) and S Mike Reid (ankle) were limited. Shough's injury, it should be noted, is to his non-throwing hand. Ford and Styles had their practice windows opened this week.Cleveland Browns at New York Jets (-1.5)DE Derek Barnett (ankle), DT Mason Graham (knee, ankle), DT Mike Hall (ankle), G Teven Jenkins (back) and WR Tylan Wallace (knee) did not practice Wednesday for Cleveland. DT Kalia Davis (quad), S Grant Delpit (shoulder) were limited. Davis and Gabriel had their practice windows opened this week.For the Jets, DB Jarvis Brownlee Jr. (concussion), RB Breece Hall (quad), LB Francisco Mauigoa (quad), WR Adonai Michell (finger) and G Dylan Parham (knee) did not participate in Wednesday's session. LB Kingsley Enagbare (knee) was the only limited participant.
Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5)The Colts listed C Tanor Bortolini (ankle), LB Jaylon Carlies (ribs), LB Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee), WR Ashton Dulin (hamstring) and DE Arden Key (hamstring) as "did not practice" on their first report of the week. RB Jonathan Taylor (NIR/rest), WR Keenan Allen (groin, NIR/rest) and CB Charvarius Ward Sr. (NIR/rest) were all limited.Three Steelers -- CB Jalen Ramsey (knee), CB Jamel Dean (ankle) and DT Cameron Heyward (NIR/rest) -- did not practice Wednesday. WR Michael Pittman (foot) and RB Rico Dowdle (toe) were limited.New York Giants at Washington Commanders (-3.5)The Giants were without DE Chauncey Golston (neck), RB Najee Harris (NIR/personal), WR Malik Nabers (knee), S Jason Pinnock (concussion), T Andrew Thomas (groin) at practice Wednesday. TE Isaiah Likely (knee, groin), TE Chris Manhertz (shoulder) and RB Cam Skattebo (shoulder) were limited.
For Washington, the most significant development, by far, was Jayden Daniels being listed as a full participant, the first time that's happened since the star quarterback suffered a dislocated elbow in Week 2 against the Cowboys. Wide receivers Terry McLaurin (hamstring) and Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice, and neither did safeties Percy Butler (hamstring) and Tyler Owens (hamstring), QB Marcis Mariota (knee) and DE Charles Omenihu (groin, ankle). The limited participants were OL Nick Allegretti (hip, Achilles), CB Trey Amos (ankle), G Sam Cosmi (concussion), RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), LB Frankie Luvu (groin), RB Jeremy McNichols (quad), TE Chig Okonkwo (hamstring), TE Ben Sinnott (rib), LB Sonny Styles (groin), RB Rachaad White (shoulder) and DE Deatrich Wise Jr. (quad). Amos, Wise and McNichols all had their practice windows opened this week.Denver Broncos (-3.5) at Los Angeles ChargersCB Pat Surtain II (ankle), CB Riley Moss (ribs) and WR Pat Bryant (ankle) did not practice Wednesday for the Broncos. DL Zach Allen (NIR/rest), OLB Deondrea Tillman (hamstring) and TE Adam Trautman (shoulder) were limited.The Chargers are dealing with a long list of ailments, including two starting tackles, Joe Alt (neck) and Rashawn Slater (ankle), both of whom didn't practice. Also not practicing were OL Trevor Penning (concussion), WR Ladd McConkey (foot), OLB Khalil Mack (NIR/rest), S Derwin James (hamstring), CB Donte Jackson (hamstring) and G Kayode Awosika (fibula). CB Cam Hart (knee), FB Alc Ingold (shoulder), WR Quentin Johnston (chest), TE Charlie Kolar (forearm), QB Trey Lance (groin), CB Deane Leonard (rib), DT Scott Matlock (foot), OT Branson Taylor (neck), WR Brenen Thompson (quad) and DE Dalvin Tomlinson (hamstring) were limited.
Detroit Lions (-5.5) at Arizona CardinalsOL Ben Bartch (foot), DL Tyleik Williams (foot) and CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) didn't practice Wednesday for the Lions. DB Brian Branch (Achilles) and C Cade Mays (wrist) were limited after having their practice windows opened. EDGE D.J. Wonnum (back) was also limited.Six Cardinals did not participate in Wednesday's practice: S Budda Baker (NIR/rest), OLB Jordan Burch (NIR/personal), OL ISaac Seumalo (NID/rest), OLB Josh Sweat (NIR/rest, groin), S Andrew Wingard (knee) and OL Isaiah Adams (ankle). RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson (back) were limited.San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5)DE Nick Bosa (knee, calf) was among several 49ers not participating in Wednesday's practice. RB Christian McCaffrey (NIR/rest), T Trent Williams (NIR/rest), LB Dre Greenlaw (NIR/rest), FB Kyle Juszczyk (knee), S Marques Sigle (ankle), CB Upton Stout (shoulder) and DT James Thompson (ankle) didn't participate, either. RB Kaelon Black (illness), WR Mike Evans (ribs) and DE Mykel Williams (knee) were limited.
The Seahawks did not have WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (NIR/rest) or LB Chazz Surratt (calf) practicing Wednesday. RB Zach Charbonnet (knee), WR Irvin Charles (knee), RB George Holani (ribs), LB Tyrice Knight (ankle), CB Nehemiah Pritchett (ankle), G Beau Stephens (knee) and DE Leonard Williams (ankle) were limited.Baltimore Ravens at Atlanta Falcons (-3.5)Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) did not practice Wednesday. Also not practicing for Baltimore were DL Calais Campbell (NIR/rest), OLB Trey Hendrickson (finger), CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring, calf), TE Durham Smythe (Achilles), T Ronnie Stanley (NIR/rest, toe, ankle) and G Andrew Vorhees (foot). Limited participants were WR Rashod Bateman (shoulder), WR Zay Flowers (foot), S Kyle Hamilton (groin), WR Chris Moore (ankle) and G John Simpson (groin).For the Falcons, OT Jake Matthews (groin), DE Za'Darius Smith (concussion, neck) and LB Yasir Abdullah (hamstring) didn't practice. OT Michael Jerrell (ankle) and DE Cameron Thomas (shoulder) were limited.
